deepDiveThesesUsed.summary: Apps advertise '60+ supported models' but the vendored llama.cpp build only recognizes specific LLM_ARCH_* tags, so many trending releases (e.g. Qwen3.x) silently can't load.

The GGUF quant label (e.g. Q4_K_M) is not a standardized artifact — different quantizers (and even a vendor's own official QAT release) produce measurably different quality/size under the identical nominal tag.

The app's July 10 Swift rewrite fixed the July 7 staleness gap by fetching llama.cpp's latest GitHub release at build time instead of a pinned old commit, but that fetch resolves 'latest' fresh every build with no pinned tag and no version ever surfaced to the user, so two builds cut hours or days apart can silently embed different sets of supported architectures with no way to tell which one shipped. Backed by real llama.cpp release-cadence data (3 tags in under 3 hours) and PR merge-time data (~1 day to 24 days depending on whether an architecture is genuinely new). Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-07 thesis: static staleness vs. dynamic non-determinism.

On-device LLM apps built on llama.cpp (Ollama, LM Studio, privateSLM's local-GGUF fallback, etc.) leave up to 10x of phone NPU throughput and up to 65% of achievable energy efficiency on the table -- not from weak silicon but from thread-scheduling, sleep-latency, and polling-interval choices in the framework layer. Backed by two independent papers (arXiv:2607.05475, submitted 2026-07-06; arXiv:2606.23001/EnerInfer, submitted 2026-06-22) plus a live, dated (2026-07-21) example inside llama.cpp's own Hexagon-NPU-backend ecosystem where a community fork currently outperforms Qualcomm's own official implementation on identical hardware.

What changed since 2026-07-09: privateslm's main branch pivoted from Flutter to a native SwiftUI + llama.cpp app on 2026-07-10 (PR #21), then shipped four rapid feature phases through 2026-07-12 (PRs #22-26: settings, live models.json catalog fetch + downloads, SwiftData chat history, TTS/voice input, Apple Intelligence engine + Siri). CRITICAL GAP: the new native engine is NOT version-pinned. scripts/fetch-llama.sh always downloads whatever is the LATEST ggml-org/llama.cpp GitHub release at build time — no tag/commit is recorded anywhere in the repo, the resulting Frameworks/llama.xcframework is gitignored (not committed), there is no CI that would capture which version went into any given build, and no App Store release/tag exists yet for the native app (README still self-describes as 'Phase 0 — engine spike', which is itself stale given Phases 1-4 already merged). This means there is currently NO reliable, checkable source of truth for which GGUF architectures the shipping engine supports — the ENGINE COMPATIBILITY hard gate (quality bar #5) cannot be verified against a stable reference. Until fetch-llama.sh is pinned to an explicit tag/commit (recorded in-repo) or a real App Store release ships with recorded engine version, catalog-compatibility checks in this routine are working from the OLD flutter-legacy llm_arch enum as the conservative fallback, since it's the only fixed, inspectable reference and it's plausible some live installs are still running that build.

Only engine-side news this week was llama.cpp build b9968 (2026-07-12) with minor OpenCL/Vulkan/schema fixes — not substantial enough alone to justify a digest per the quality bar (no shipped-model-relevant datapoint).
